scope: An exploratory visual taxonomy, not an exhaustive encyclopedia or a claim that visual qualities have sole inventors.

methods.name: Perlin noise
methods.roleDescription: Produces a spatial field from coordinates.
methods.mechanism: Interpolate dot products between lattice gradients and the offsets to a sample point. Nearby samples vary smoothly.
methods.implementation: A seeded 2D gradient-noise implementation with eight gradient directions and quintic interpolation. One octave, mapped to color; not the exact 1985 or 2002 reference code, fBm, or a fluid simulation.
methods.canvasDescription: A continuous violet and cream field. Increasing lattice cells makes the variations smaller and more frequent.

methods.name: Gaussian blur
methods.mechanism: Replace each pixel with a weighted neighborhood average. A Gaussian kernel gives nearer pixels more weight; sigma sets its spread.
methods.implementation: Actual separable convolution of a 128 × 112 grayscale image. The sampled kernel is normalized, truncated at ±3σ, and applied horizontally then vertically with clamped edges. Sigma is measured in source pixels.
methods.canvasDescription: The same geometric image before and after filtering. Increasing sigma softens edges and removes fine detail; zero leaves it unchanged.

eponym.name: Carl Friedrich Gauss
eponym.note: The Gaussian name connects to the mathematical distribution. It does not credit Gauss with inventing digital image blur. A digital-filter contribution record is still an open research item here.

methods.name: L-systems
methods.roleDescription: Rewrites symbols, then interprets them as geometry.
methods.mechanism: Rewrite every eligible symbol in parallel, generation by generation. A turtle reads the resulting string as moves, turns, and saved branch positions.
methods.implementation: A deterministic bracketed L-system: axiom F; production F → F[+F]F[−F]F; four rewriting generations. + and − turn; brackets push and restore turtle state. The drawing is fitted to the frame after each change.
methods.canvasDescription: A line structure repeatedly branches from one trunk. Increasing the turn angle opens the branching geometry.

sources.label: The Algorithmic Beauty of Plants · author archive

methods.name: Moiré
methods.mechanism: Superimpose two line grids with a small angular difference. Their local alignments produce larger apparent bands.
methods.implementation: Two equally spaced, straight-line grids; one stays fixed while the other rotates. This illustrates geometric interference, not a reconstruction of a named artwork. Display scaling can add screen-sampling artifacts.
methods.canvasDescription: Two grids of thin violet lines overlap to form wider bands. Rotating one grid changes the spacing and direction of those bands.

methods.name: Ordered dithering
methods.roleDescription: Represents continuous tone with discrete marks.
methods.mechanism: Compare each input value against a threshold from a repeating matrix. Each output pixel becomes one of two values, while the local pattern suggests intermediate tones.
methods.implementation: A 4 × 4 Bayer threshold matrix, applied to a generated grayscale field. The output has exactly two colors. This is ordered dithering, not Floyd–Steinberg error diffusion or random-dot dithering.
methods.canvasDescription: A smooth tonal image at left becomes a regular two-color pixel pattern at right. Brightness changes the density of dark pixels.
